prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: Monthly mean ozone by monitoring station (language en).
Grid: 13 columns × 7 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Station" · longest unbreakable word 73px · one-line width 73px
  col 2: header "Jan" · longest unbreakable word 31px · one-line width 31px
  col 3: header "Feb" · longest unbreakable word 31px · one-line width 31px
  col 4: header "Mar" · longest unbreakable word 31px · one-line width 31px
  col 5: header "Apr" · longest unbreakable word 32px · one-line width 32px
  col 6: header "May" · longest unbreakable word 32px · one-line width 32px
  col 7: header "Jun" · longest unbreakable word 31px · one-line width 31px
  col 8: header "Jul" · longest unbreakable word 32px · one-line width 32px
  col 9: header "Aug" · longest unbreakable word 32px · one-line width 32px
  col 10: header "Sep" · longest unbreakable word 32px · one-line width 32px
  col 11: header "Oct" · longest unbreakable word 32px · one-line width 32px
  col 12: header "Nov" · longest unbreakable word 31px · one-line width 31px
  col 13: header "Dec" · longest unbreakable word 31px · one-line width 31px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 360px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 359px.
This table cannot fit without splitting words at 360px. You MAY choose a total wider than 359px (the reader then scrolls horizontally), or squeeze and accept splits — a design decision.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"Compare monthly mean ozone levels across six monitoring stations and reveal each station's seasonal profile.","reading":"Readers find a station in column 1, then scan horizontally across Jan–Dec to see its seasonal rise and fall; they may also compare one month vertically across stations. The month sequence is the main comparative axis.","groups":["col 1 Station: row identifier, separate from the measurements","cols 2–13 Jan–Dec: one homogeneous 12-month numeric series; quarters Jan–Mar, Apr–Jun, Jul–Sep, Oct–Dec are conceptual subgroups but all months should share a common width"],"keep_intact":["col 1 station names and the Station header","cols 2–13 month abbreviations Jan–Dec","all one-decimal numeric values and their decimal points"],"may_wrap":["None naturally: station names, month labels and values are single unbreakable tokens; any wrapping is forced splitting. If forced, station names can use extra row height better than numeric cells can."]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r0A: widths [94, 52, 52, 52, 53, 53, 52, 53, 53, 53, 53, 52, 52] · table 725×255px · row heights [36, 36, 36, 36, 36, 36, 36] · column headers wrapped 0/13 · tallest cell 1 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 365px
Design r0B: widths [73, 52, 52, 52, 53, 53, 52, 53, 53, 53, 53, 52, 52] · table 704×348px · row heights [36, 60, 60, 36, 60, 60, 36] · column headers wrapped 0/13 · tallest cell 2 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 344px
Design r0C: widths [94, 38, 38, 38, 38, 38, 38, 38, 38, 38, 38, 38, 38] · table 551×580px · row heights [83, 83, 83, 83, 83, 83, 83] · column headers wrapped 12/13 · tallest cell 3 lines · mid-word splits 136 · OVERFLOWS the box by 191px
Constraint adjustments applied: r0C: raised a column to the minimum 38px; raised a column to the minimum 38px; raised a column to the minimum 38px; raised a column to the minimum 38px; raised a column to the minimum 38px; raised a column to the minimum 38px; raised a column to the minimum 38px; raised a column to the minimum 38px; raised a column to the minimum 38px; raised a column to the minimum 38px; raised a column to the minimum 38px; raised a column to the minimum 38px

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}

log.raw: {"critique":[{"design":"r0A","good":"All 13 columns stay on one line: station names, month headers, and one-decimal values are intact; row heights are a uniform 36px and the horizontal scan across months is clean.
